state_limits: Parent gitlink equals child HEAD; bounded git status --short --untracked-files=normal was clean. Corpus inputs are external; no source was compiled and no notebook or model ran.
description: A tokenizer research scratchpad experiments with capped n-gram vocabulary construction, count/reduction heuristics, a CUDA port, and notebook conversion to HuggingFace tokenizer JSON.
scope_audience: The stated audience is the author exploring bounded-vocabulary token construction rather than a maintained tokenizer library or existing consumer.

creativity.reason: Reducing an overfull n-gram set by shortening low-value grams is an interesting alternative to iterating a standard merge loop; global novelty and comparative quality remain unknown.

current_usefulness.reason: The C++ implementations and JSON-export notebook are concrete research material, but the README says there are no consumers, required corpora/intermediates are absent, and one listed source is not buildable.

expected_usefulness.reason: If the bounded-vocabulary method yields a correct, reproducible tokenizer pipeline, it could be useful to researchers with a fixed vocabulary budget; no quality or speed benefit is demonstrated.

impl_progress.reason: The CPU code implements threaded gram counting and heap-based reduction, with a CUDA counterpart and conversion notebooks; no tests, build system, or inspected output establishes end-to-end correctness.

presentability.reason: README explains the intent, command forms, notebook order, missing corpora, and archive limits, but lacks a unified build or reproducible example.

delivery_likelihood.reason: Some files have direct compile commands, but input corpora are absent, several variants are scratch code, and no build or output has been checked.

verification: Inspected README and representative C++ counting/reduction implementations. No compilation, corpus access, tests, or notebook execution.

evidence.locator: What; Why it exists; How to run; Status

contribution: A family of experiments bounds a working n-gram lexicon by pruning and shortening low-scoring entries, then attempts to emit a tokenizer model representation.
alternatives_question: Which tokenizer-building systems use bounded n-gram counting and reduction rather than iterative BPE or unigram training, and how do they compare on token quality and resource use with the same corpus and vocabulary cap?
reason: The authored algorithm is more than an idea, but missing inputs, absent validation, and no comparative result keep its utility and readiness provisional.
next_step: Use a small distributable corpus and independently check count/reduction invariants, tokenizer export, and quality against standard baselines at the same vocabulary cap.
